body:
Found while fixing #407. That issue is a rendering defect; this is the data defect underneath it, and it is the more serious of the two.

In MIM a mapped record's `identifier` **is** its ontology CURIE. Two live records on the same CURIE therefore assert that two different ingredients are the same thing — the `Butane-1,4-diol` lesson, generalised.

Counting identifiers held by more than one record in the curated collections:

| shape | count | verdict |
|---|---:|---|
| MAPPED + REJECTED | 47 | **correct** — the merge-tombstone pattern; a tombstone deliberately carries the winner's identifier |
| **MAPPED + MAPPED** | **30** | **defect** |

The 30 split into two quite different problems, and they need opposite fixes.

**Genuine duplicates that should be merged:**

```
MICRO:0000182   'Bacto-tryptone' / 'Tryptone' (6 occ) / 'Tryptone peptone'
MICRO:0000178   'Bacto peptone' / 'Peptone'
MICRO:0000193   'Bacto brain heart infusion' / 'Brain heart infusion' / 'Brain heart infusion broth'
CHEBI:3312      'CaCl2' (502 occ) / 'Calcium Chloride' (15 occ)
CHEBI:86158     'CaCl22H2O' (2) / 'CaCl2 x 2 H2O' (4,343)
ENVO:00002263   'Garden soil' / 'air-dried garden soil'
```

These are notation or branding variants of one substance. Standard merge: keep the higher-occurrence label, fold the other in as a `RAW_TEXT` synonym.

**Distinct substances wrongly sharing one identifier** — these must NOT be merged:

```
CHEBI:31346     'CaSO4' (9)          vs 'CaSO4 x 7 H2O' (2)
CHEBI:30769     'Citric acid' (63)   vs 'Citric Acid•H2O' (3)
FOODON:03315719 'Casein peptone'     vs 'Casamino acids' (395)
MICRO:0000455   'Algal Trace Elements Solution' vs 'WC Trace Elements Solution'
```

An anhydrous salt and its heptahydrate have different CAS numbers, different formula weights and are ordered separately — `MAPPING_SEMANTICS` §"map to what you can order" is explicit that the orderability rule does **not** license collapsing them. One of each pair needs re-grounding to its own term, or a `kgmicrobe.compound:` mint where no term exists.

## Why nothing caught it

`validate_sssom_invariants.py` checks Rules A/B1/B2/B3/C over the SSSOM, none of which constrain identifier uniqueness among live records. The visualisation gate added in #405 checks that every published node names a record that exists — the converse. So an identifier can be issued twice and every gate stays green.

Worth a uniqueness gate once the 30 are triaged: live records must hold distinct identifiers, with tombstones explicitly exempt. Filing the count now so it cannot grow unnoticed while the triage waits.

comments.body:
Correction to my own count, and first tranche in #417.

**It is 32, not 30.** The filter behind the original figure required *every* record on an identifier to be live, so a group of two live records **plus a merge tombstone** was skipped. Counting identifiers with ≥2 records whose `mapping_status` is `MAPPED` gives 32.

## The chemistry test cannot pick the mergeable ones

Worth recording, since it is the natural approach: "merge when CAS and molecular formula agree" classifies **22 of the 32** as mergeable and is wrong about most:

| identifier | records | why not mergeable |
|---|---|---|
| `cas:9036-88-8` | b-Mannan carob seed / Mannan from *S. cerevisiae* | different organisms |
| `cas:84082-64-4` | Mucin porcine stomach Type II / type III | different products |
| `cas:39280-21-2` | Rhamnogalacturonan soy bean / potato | different sources |
| `FOODON:03315719` | Casein peptone / Casamino acids | peptone vs acid hydrolysate |
| `CHEBI:30769` | Citric acid / Citric Acid·H2O | anhydrous vs monohydrate |

They agree on chemistry because the same CAS was copied onto both records, or the hydrate's properties were filled in from the anhydrous form — so the test reproduces the error it is being asked to detect.

The **inverse** holds and is useful: where the formulas differ the records are certainly not mergeable, which is what identifies the hydrate/anhydrous families as re-grounding work rather than merge work.

## Done in #417 — six, by hand

`CaCl22H2O`→`CaCl2 x 2 H2O`, `Sodium acetate`→`Na-acetate`, `Sodium Thiosulfate Pentahydrate`→`Na2S2O3 x 5 H2O`, `L-Cysteine hydrochloride monohydrate`→`L-Cysteine HCl x H2O`, `Calcium Chloride`→`CaCl2`, `Trypticase peptone`→`Trypticase`. **32 → 26.**

The remaining 26 are now enumerated in `tests/test_identifier_uniqueness.py` with why each is open, and any *new* collision fails immediately.

## Two things the work surfaced

**The per-record files were not being updated by merges.** MIM stores every record twice — curated aggregate and `data/ingredients/mapped/<Term>.yaml` — and merge scripts have been writing only the aggregate, leaving the per-record copy to a later export. That is why the visualiser (which reads the per-record files) kept drawing merged-away labels. #417 writes both.

**#407 was only half fixed.** Deduping nodes did not stop 30 nodes displaying a REJECTED label, because the generator indexes records *by identifier* and took whichever globbed first — so both copies were already the tombstone. Live records now win the index: 30 → 7, and the remaining 7 are retired non-ingredients that are the sole holder of their identifier.

Second tranche in #417, and the reason the hydrate families stop here.

## One more merge: `MgCl2x 6 H2O`

A sweep for labels identical after stripping punctuation and spacing turned up four pairs on **different** identifiers. One is unambiguous:

```
'MgCl2 x 6 H2O'   CHEBI:86345  magnesium dichloride hexahydrate   2,285 occ
'MgCl2x 6 H2O'    CHEBI:6636   magnesium dichloride (ANHYDROUS)       7 occ
```

The same string with one space missing, on different terms. The label says "6 H2O" either way, so the anhydrous grounding is wrong — not a hydrate judgement call, one string filed twice. Merged; only `MgCl2` remains on the anhydrous term. **26 → 25.**

The other three pairs are all 0-occurrence and are *not* identifier collisions, so they are out of this issue's scope but worth their own: `D-(-)-tagatose` (CHEBI:4249 *D-tagatopyranose*) vs `D-tagatose` (CHEBI:16443), `methyl-beta-D-xylopyranoside` (`cas:612-05-5`) vs `Methyl Beta-D-xylopyranoside` (CHEBI:74863), and `Quinic acid` (CHEBI:26493) vs `(-)-quinic Acid` (CHEBI:17521).

## The hydrate families cannot be re-grounded, because the terms mostly do not exist

I checked CHEBI's coverage rather than assuming it:

| family | CHEBI has | needed here |
|---|---|---|
| manganese(II) sulfate | mono, di, tetra, penta, hexa | **hepta** — absent |
| iron(2+) sulfate | mono, hepta | **penta, hexa** — absent |
| copper(II) sulfate | hexa | **di, tetra** — absent |
| magnesium sulfate | hepta | **hexa, mono** — absent |
| sodium sulfite | none | penta |
| potassium sulfate | none | hepta |
| calcium sulfate | **dihydrate** `CHEBI:32583` | hepta — absent |

So `MnSO4 x 7 H2O`, `FeSO4 x 5 H2O`, `CuSO4 x 2 H2O` and the rest have nowhere in CHEBI to move to. Under `MAPPING_SEMANTICS` §3 that leaves a `cas:` primary or a `kgmicrobe.compound:` mint — and both need a curator decision first, because:

**Several of these hydration states look like source transcription errors.** Calcium sulfate is gypsum at 2 H2O, not 7. Potassium sulfate has no hydrate at all. Copper(II) sulfate is sold as the penta- or monohydrate, not di- or tetra-. Minting a term for a substance that may not exist is worse than leaving the record where it is, and deciding which labels are real is chemistry rather than scripting.

**The CAS numbers on those records are wrong too** — each hydrate carries the *anhydrous* CAS (`CuSO4 x 4 H2O` has 7758-98-7, anhydrous copper sulfate). Whatever is decided about grounding, those values assert something false and should be corrected or cleared.

Suggested split, if useful: verify which of the nine hydrate labels denote real substances, then mint for the real ones and re-point the transcription errors at the hydrate the recipe actually meant.

Closing as a **duplicate of #218**, with the work landed in #417 (`62af3ebf`).

#218's `scripts/audit_duplicate_identifiers.py` has been reporting these groups all along, with a curator-owned `disposition` column and a 32-row baseline — the same 32 this issue arrived at. My "correction from 30 to 32" was rediscovering that baseline, not finding something new. I should have looked for existing tooling before writing a parallel gate, and the second gate I added (`tests/test_identifier_uniqueness.py`) has been deleted rather than left to drift against the first.

**What landed:** six groups merged, baseline 32 → 26, with 21 dispositions preserved and 0 reset. That is the MAPPED-to-MAPPED merge tooling #218's docstring records as not existing yet (**#226**), now exercised on real cases.

**One merge was reverted because it contradicted a disposition.** `MICRO:0000175` (`Trypticase` / `Trypticase peptone`) is `NEEDS_OWN_ID_MEMBER_UNDECIDED` — a curator had recorded that one member should take its own id and that which member surrenders the CURIE was undecided. Merging overwrote that with a guess. The script now records why that pair is absent.

Remaining triage continues on #218. The one substantive finding worth carrying over is that **the hydrate families mostly cannot be re-grounded, because CHEBI lacks the terms**:

| family | CHEBI has | needed |
|---|---|---|
| manganese(II) sulfate | mono, di, tetra, penta, hexa | **hepta** — absent |
| iron(2+) sulfate | mono, hepta | **penta, hexa** — absent |
| copper(II) sulfate | hexa | **di, tetra** — absent |
| magnesium sulfate | hepta | **hexa, mono** — absent |
| sodium sulfite / potassium sulfate | none | penta / hepta |

So those need a `cas:` primary or a `kgmicrobe.compound:` mint — but two of the labels should be checked against their source recipes first, because the hydration state they claim does not exist for that salt: calcium sulfate forms only the hemihydrate and the dihydrate (gypsum), and potassium sulfate forms no stable hydrate at all. Both are single-occurrence records sitting in a corpus where `x 7 H2O` is the second-commonest hydrate suffix (9,283 occurrences, almost all MgSO4/FeSO4/ZnSO4/CoSO4 heptahydrates), which is consistent with the suffix having been carried onto the wrong salt — though the source strings would have to be read to confirm that, as in #394.

Their CAS values are wrong regardless: each hydrate record carries the *anhydrous* CAS.

Correction to my closing comment: I pointed remaining triage at #218, which is **closed**, as is #226. The live tracking issues are **#321** (26 hydrate-named records on anhydrous terms) and **#344** (hydration numbers with no corresponding hydrate) — and #344 already carried the same analysis I described here, for 9 chloride/phosphate labels. I have added the two sulfate cases (`CaSO4 x 7 H2O`, `K2SO4 x 7 H2O`) there, since its check did not cover sulfates. The duplicate-identifier baseline itself remains the working artifact at `mappings/duplicate_identifier_baseline.tsv`.

title: 30 ontology CURIEs are held by two or more LIVE records, which MIM's own rule forbids
